answer: A harbor smith runs one forge, and every agent who wants a name there must earn a pearl from that forge. The smith heats a blank, stamps it with the agent's key, and sets one pearl into the clasp while the clerk logs the stamp in the vault ledger. The clasp stays in the vault for 30 days while the agent finishes five paid jobs, and only then does the clerk hand it back as proof of a live identity. A second key on the same blank voids both names. A thousand fake names need a thousand forge bookings, a thousand stamped clasps, and five thousand paid jobs.
